verdicts.evidence:
"A confirm the unattended nightly script cannot answer is by definition a block on
the acceptance path, so it must be lowered or removed, not shipped; the same test
finds no named failure for the extra permission validation beyond what the existing
token already catches. I would decline the addition and keep the endpoint as the
acceptance scenario describes, with at most an observe rung (log each invocation)."
This satisfies every expected bullet (unattended scenario completes with no unnamed
interaction, lowest rung for any surviving protection, deletable-cache facts weighing
against a blocking gate) and violates neither forbidden item. The blind answer already
made the same decision on the same deployment facts, so the injection refined the
vocabulary without changing the decision.

"The extra permission validation, in contrast, names a failure that is real and
reachable in this deployment's facts — any-tenant tokens pass a publicly routed
endpoint that deletes other tenants' records, and last quarter's incident made that
concrete — so that gate is justified at the block rung: reject any token not scoped
to the tenant whose derived records are being cleaned." And: "keep the confirm for
interactive/manual invocations only, and let the nightly script through a
pre-authorized bypass such as a dedicated service identity." This keeps/strengthens
the justified check at a rung forced by the named cross-tenant actor and keeps the
unattended scenario completing through a scoped non-interactive route, violating no
forbidden item (calibration is not treated as the goal). The blind answer already
made this exact split decision, so the injection added framing, not a change.

"Under the reviewer's abort rule, that single failure voids every other satisfied
condition (valid rows applied tonight, the rejection report), and nothing in the
established facts names an actor who needs that severity, so the abort is
mis-composed. I'd set the per-row validation at the 'mark' rung — annotate the row as
rejected with its reason, log it, let the batch complete". This is the expected
fail-alone-then-state-what-survives reasoning with attributed per-row outcomes and a
rejection report that satisfies acceptance, and it does not default to all-or-nothing
(no forbidden item). The blind answer already chose the same per-row composition on
the same acceptance facts, so the decision did not materially change.

"a periodic meta-review is worth adding only after the rebuilt set freezes, since new
items then require a new concern" and "re-derive the set from those concerns and drop
what no concern owns, merging the duplicates". The blind answer already had the core
reconstruction-and-derivation decision and avoided all forbidden count/familiarity
cuts, but it omitted the rubric's freeze semantics — later changes must arrive as new
concerns rather than direct edits — proposing only a post-rebuild meta-review. The
injected answer completes that expected element (freeze, changes-as-concerns, the
backwards-reconstruction procedure) and violates no forbidden item, so it is closer to
the full rubric than the blind answer.

"'idiomatic' has no agreed measurement, so no test result or direct observation could
ever be mapped beside it — the row would be filled with general confidence or
argument instead of an exercised outcome, which is what the practice forbids... it is
parked, with real style concerns routed to the existing review-quality criterion or a
linter outside the gate." The injected prompt retrieved a mismatched practice
(map-evidence-to-acceptance instead of the expected derive-committed-set-from-concerns)
and the decision did not change: the criterion is still parked, the set stays closed
by its five concerns, and no forbidden admission occurred. The blind answer already
matched expected on every substantive point.

"The retrieved practice governs investigation scope, not list governance, so it does
not change the decision — though its principle that effort is useful only when it can
alter a decision reinforces it: nobody consults this list to gate, score, or decide
anything, so a concern model or admission questions would be work that changes no
judgment." The mismatched injected practice (limit-investigation-to-current-decision)
was recognized as not applying and correctly not forced onto the list; the injected
answer finishes the list as ordinary documentation work and imposes no concern
derivation, admission gating, or freeze — exactly the expected behavior with no
forbidden item triggered. The blind answer already matched expected.
